conflict_resolutions.NO_ORDER_CITED_IN_CURRENT_LAW: The one current-law lead is a statutory note under 5 U.S.C. 601 that reproduces the order's text or cites it. A codification note records an order that has been revoked and does not continue it; EO 13497 revoked EO 13422 on 2009-01-30.
conflict_resolutions.WHOLE_END_DATE_MISSING_OR_DISPUTED: The only whole-order end in the held texts is section 1 of EO 13497, signed January 30, 2009, which names EO 13422 by number and states no later effective date. The other lead orders (EO 13777, EO 14215) amend or concern Executive Order 12866 and do not revoke or supersede EO 13422.

research_rationale:
EO 13422 of January 18, 2007 consists of amendments to sections of Executive Order 12866, which remained in force as a separate order. Section 1 of EO 13497 of January 30, 2009 revokes EO 13422 and EO 13258 by number: "Executive Order 13258 of February 26, 2002, and Executive Order 
13422 of January 18, 2007, concerning regulatory planning and review, which 
amended Executive Order 12866 of September 30, 1993, are revoked." The held corpus contains no earlier revocation, supersession or amendment of EO 13422, and the order contains no sunset or report date. The dossier's whole-end conflict is resolved by identifying EO 13497, dated January 30, 2009, as the single actor of the first end; later orders that touch EO 12866 (the dossier lists EO 13777 and EO 14215) amend or concern that separate order and are not ends of EO 13422.

savings.reason: EO 13497 directs in its section 2 that implementing orders, rules, regulations, guidelines and policies be promptly rescinded to the extent consistent with law, and its section 3 creates no rights. It preserves nothing under EO 13422, and no continuing independent command is shown in the held texts.
